title: Maximum Total Area Occupied by Pistons
statement:
An engine has `n` pistons, each sliding on a track from position `0` up to position `height`. Piston `i` starts at `positions[i]`, and the area under it always equals its current position. `directions[i]` is `'U'` when piston `i` is moving up and `'D'` when it is moving down.

Every second, all pistons move one unit at the same time, each in its current direction. A piston that sits at an end (position `0` or `height`) reverses before it moves, so it never leaves the track: from `height` it always moves down next, and from `0` it always moves up next, even if its letter in `directions` says otherwise.

The total area is the sum of all piston positions. Return the largest total area at any whole second, counting the starting moment (second 0).
signature: long maxArea(int height, int[] positions, String directions)
notes:
## Intuition

Every piston bounces between `0` and `height`, so after `2 * height` seconds each one is back where it started, moving the same way: one full cycle contains every possible total. Moving every piston every second would cost O(n · height). Instead, note that each second the total changes by (pistons moving up) − (pistons moving down). This `slope` only changes when a piston turns around, at most twice per piston per cycle, so a difference array of turning moments lets the cycle be replayed in O(1) per second.

## Approach

1. Let `period = 2 * height` and create `turns`, where `turns[t]` is how much the slope changes at second `t`.
2. For each piston, add its `position` to `area`. A piston moving up adds 1 to `slope`, turns down at second `height - position` (−2) and up again at `period - position` (+2). A piston moving down subtracts 1, turns up at second `position` (+2) and down at `height + position` (−2).
3. `best` starts as the area at second 0.
4. For each `time` from 0 to `period - 1`, add `turns[time]` to `slope`, then `slope` to `area` (the area one second later), and keep the maximum in `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`height = 5`, so `period = 10`. Piston 0 (at 2, up) gives `area = 2`, `slope = 1` and turns at seconds 3 (−2) and 8 (+2). Piston 1 (at 5, down) gives `area = 7`, `slope = 0` and turns at seconds 5 (+2) and 10 (−2, past the replay). Replaying: seconds 1 to 3 keep area 7; at `time = 3` the slope becomes −2 (areas 5, 3); at `time = 5` it is 0 again (3, 3, 3); at `time = 8` it is +2 (5, 7). Nothing beats the starting 7, so `best = 7`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + height): one pass over the pistons and one over the `2 * height` seconds.
- Space: O(height) for `turns`.

## Pitfalls

- A piston at `height` marked `'U'` (or at `0` marked `'D'`) turns at second 0: apply `turns[time]` before moving.
- A turn changes the slope by 2: the piston stops adding 1 and starts subtracting 1.
- Second 0 counts, so `best` starts from the initial area.
- Totals reach about 10^11, beyond 32-bit integers; use `long` in Java and C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `period` | length of one full cycle, `2 * height` seconds |
| `turns` | `turns[t]` is the change of `slope` at second `t` |
| `area` | total area at the current second |
| `slope` | change of `area` per second: pistons moving up minus pistons moving down |
| `position` | the current piston's starting position |
| `best` | largest total area seen so far |
| `time` | the second being replayed |
